generatedBy: tools/mp-nano-extractor --prof 9 (nanos.ocp) plus its diagnostic function dump for every one of the 159 ids and for the 16 child nanos they cast, joined to enforcer-nano-sources.json. Prose is curated; every id, name, number, nano line, strain, level, cast requirement and cast target is read from the client data.
purpose: Every nano an Enforcer can cast, in exactly ONE section, with the nanoline (= stacking strain) on every row so a bot or a player can see what overwrites what. The Enforcer's kit is taunts, Mongo rage HP and Absorb / damage-shield layers, so those three are enumerated to the last nano.

dataSources.castability: A nano is Enforcer-castable when a ToUse action (ActionType 3) carries Profession(60)==9 OR VisualProfession(368)==9. 70 of the 159 gate via Profession(60), 89 via VisualProfession(368).
dataSources.castTarget: Read from the nano's own effect functions: Target(3) = castable on another character, Wearer(2)/User(1) = self only. Where a nano has several functions, the target of its stat-modifying functions (53045/53012/53110/53026) decides.

howEnforcerBuffsStack.rule: Two nanos in the SAME nanoline (NanoStrain, stat 75) never coexist: the newer replaces the older regardless of which is stronger. Two nanos in DIFFERENT nanolines always stack. The nanoLine field on every row below is that strain, read from the nano itself - it is the authoritative stacking key, not the nano's name or its category.
theTraps: TRAP 1 - Mongo's X and Essence of X are the SAME line. Both are HPBuff(151). The Mongo's line (9 ids, self only, up to Max Health +20000 on Mongo's Kraken) and the Essence line (8 ids, cast on ANY target, up to Max Health +1998 on Improved Essence of Behemoth) cannot both be on one character. An Enforcer who buffs himself with an Essence throws away his own Mongo's; a teammate re-buffed by a second Enforcer loses the first one's.

TRAP 2 - Ice Burn does not stack with the damage shields. Ice Burn (269460) is DamageShields(1), the same line as all 15 'Avenging Shield -> Coruscating Screen' shields. Casting the Shadowlands proc-shield removes the reflective shield and vice versa.

TRAP 3 - Superior Fortify is self-only and sits in the TEAM Absorb line. Superior Fortify (273320) is AbsorbACBuff(219), the same line as the 10 'Thicken Skin -> Greater Fortify' absorbs the Enforcer casts on other people. It is Wearer-targeted, so an Enforcer running it cannot also carry a teammate's Absorb, and casting Greater Fortify on himself drops it.

TRAP 4 - every Challenger switches the Enforcer's nano casting off. All 19 Challenger(5) nanos end in CastNano[157742] or CastNano[157743], both named 'Nano skills inoperative', both applying -4000 to all six nano schools (Sensory Improvement 122, Matter Metamorphosis 127, Biological Metamorphosis 128, Psychological Modification 129, Matter Creation 130, Time & Space 131). While Challenger is up the Enforcer cannot cast anything else, so every other buff has to go up FIRST.

TRAP 5 - Rage costs healing. All 6 Rage(189) nanos apply a negative HealReactivity (stat 689): -5 on Berserk Rage up to -50 on Hellish Rage. They also strip roots, snares and stuns via RemoveNanoStrain. The Mongo's line goes the other way and gives HealReactivity +20, so the two pull against each other.

TRAP 6 - the melee weapon buffs split across targets INSIDE one line. MeleeWeaponBuffLine(180) holds 25 nanos: 23 are Wearer (self only, the Shadowlands 'Thugs Glory / Skill of the Reaper' ladder) and 2 are Target (Brutal Thug 29630 and Headcracker 29644, the old Rubi-Ka buffs an Enforcer can put on someone else). A teammate who receives Brutal Thug loses whatever other strain-180 buff he had.

TRAP 7 - the single-target taunts are strain 0 (NOSTACKING). NanoLine 0 is not a stacking line at all: each taunt is an instant TauntNpc effect that lands on its own. They never collide with each other or with anything else, so the only reason to cast a smaller one is nano cost.
howEnforcerBuffsStack.nanodeckGate: 7 nanos carry a NanoFocusLevel BitAnd 64 requirement in their ToUse criteria - the Enforcer Nanodeck gate. They are the top of their lines and are uncastable without it: Hellish Rage (275830), Improved Element of Malice (275014), Improved Essence of Behemoth (273629), Mongo Demolish! (270786), Mongo's Kraken (273322), Superior Fortify (273320), Valiant Challenger to Behemoth (275833).
howEnforcerBuffsStack.specializationGate: 22 nanos carry a Specialization BitAnd requirement (1/2/4/8 = first through fourth specialisation). They are the Shadowlands ladder: the Mongo's line above Mongo's Titan, the Spite -> Element of Malice taunts, the Fearbringer -> Dreadbringer procs and all six Element of <damage type> nanos.

tauntsAndAggro.note: 18 of the Enforcer's 159 nanos exist to take and hold aggro. Every single-target taunt is strain 0 (NOSTACKING), i.e. an instant effect that never overwrites anything. The Mongo line is the AoE half: the nano the Enforcer casts hits HIMSELF for a fixed amount of Health and then area-casts a CHILD nano (strain 1037, 'Taunt') on everything within 20m - and that child's taunt value is chosen at cast time from three Psychological Modification bands. Those child ids and bands are read out of nanos.ocp and listed below; the parent nano contains NO taunt number at all.

wantedFromOthers.effect: Raises every weapon skill and every nano skill at once for a few minutes.
wantedFromOthers.note: The Enforcer's six nano schools all cost 2.5 - its joint most expensive tier, from reference/skillcaps.json - while its top nanos need Psychological Modification 1534 (Improved Element of Malice), Biological Metamorphosis 1533 and Matter Creation 1533 (Mongo's Kraken, Improved Essence of Behemoth). A wrangle is how most Enforcers reach those without capping the schools.

Mechanically load-bearing for this class. ZERO of the Enforcer's 159 nanos contain a heal function; the only thing in its kit that touches healing is a PENALTY (the Rage line's HealReactivity -5 to -50). A raiding Enforcer's survivability is Mongo HP + Absorb + shields + someone else's heals.

The Enforcer has NO AC buff of its own. Its defensive kit is Absorb (line 219, stats 238-245) and reflective Shield AC (line 1, stats 226-234) - different stats from plain AC, so an Engineer's or MP's armour buff stacks on top of everything in this file.

selfBuffCastOrder: 1. Mongo's X, highest rank castable - it is the health pool everything else is measured against, and it is self-only.
2. Superior Fortify (273320) if the Enforcer Nanodeck is worn, else the best line-219 Absorb the Enforcer can put on himself.
3. Ice Burn (269460) if Shadowlands, else the best damage shield from line 1 - they are the SAME line, pick one.
4. The weapon buff for the weapon actually held: line 180 for 1hB/1hE/2hB/2hE, Vlad's Revenge (202858) for Piercing (line 278), Call of the Maelstorm (203215) for Melee Energy (line 279).
5. The best self-castable Fervor (line 519) and the best Element of <type> (line 597).
7. Challenger LAST - once it lands the Enforcer cannot cast anything else until it drops (TRAP 4).
Rage is NOT in this order: it is a reactive break-free, and its HealReactivity penalty makes it wrong to leave running.
aggroRotation: Opening a pull: the biggest single-target taunt the Enforcer can cast (line 0, no stacking cost).
Adds, or a team member pulling aggro: a Mongo (line 188). Choose by Health cost against current Health - Mongo Slam! costs 12 Health, Mongo Demolish! costs 550.
The Mongo child taunt scales with Psychological Modification, so a bot must read its own PsyMod and know which of the three bands it is in before choosing a Mongo.
The taunt proc (line 627) covers aggro between casts for free while auto-attacking.
Mongo Rampage! (204199) is the emergency AoE-aura option, at the cost of Run Speed -700 - it pins the Enforcer in place.
whatNotToDo: Never cast an Essence on yourself - it replaces your own Mongo's X (TRAP 1).
Never cast a damage shield while Ice Burn is up, or vice versa (TRAP 2).
Never cast a team Absorb on yourself while Superior Fortify is up (TRAP 3).
Never cast Challenger before the rest of the buff set (TRAP 4).
Do not keep Rage up as a maintenance buff (TRAP 5).

coverage.note: Every one of the 159 Enforcer-castable nanos appears in exactly one section. Line-summary rows carry representativeId + representativeName and list every id they cover in coversNanoIds, so no id is hidden behind a label.

_deviations: NO PETS. enforcer-pets.json is deliberately absent: no SummonPet function appears in any of the 159 Enforcer-castable nanos. 'enforcer' is already present in the renderer's PETLESS list in tools/aodb/app.py, so the Pets tab correctly states the class has no pets and no app.py change was needed.

NO HEALS AT ALL. The Soldier and Doctor templates both carry a Heals/HoT section. The Enforcer has none - zero of its 159 nanos contain a heal function. enforcer-nanos.json files Mongo Rampage! (204199) under 'Heals / HoT' because its Max Health +6000 looks like one to the generic classifier; it is an AoE taunt aura and is placed under tauntsAndAggro here.

NO AC BUFF AND NO REFLECT. Where the Soldier's defensive kit is reflect (ShadowlandReflectBase) plus armour buffs (ArmorBuff line 3), the Enforcer has neither. Its two defensive lines are Absorb (AbsorbACBuff 219, stats 238-245) and reflective damage shields (DamageShields 1, stats 226-234). Nothing here touches plain AC except as a side bonus on the shields.

THE SIGNATURE SELF-BUFF AND THE SIGNATURE TEAM BUFF ARE THE SAME STRAIN. HPBuff(151) holds BOTH the Enforcer's own Mongo's line (9 nanos, target User) and the Essence line it gives away (8 nanos, target Target). No other finished class has its headline self-buff and its headline team buff colliding like this; it is TRAP 1 and it drives the whole bot cast order.

THE TOP SELF-BUFF DISABLES ITS OWN CASTING. Every Challenger(5) rank ends in CastNano[157742/157743] 'Nano skills inoperative' = -4000 to all six nano schools. No other finished class has a buff that locks out its own nano kit, and it turns the buff SET into a buff ORDER.

TAUNT VALUES ARE NOT IN THE PARENT NANO. The Mongo line's parent carries only the Health cost and an AreaCastNano; the actual TauntNpc number lives in a child nano (strain 1037) and is picked at cast time from three Psychological Modification bands. Reading only the parent - which is what enforcer-nanos.json effectSummary shows - reports the Mongo line as having no taunt at all. The child ids and bands were pulled from nanos.ocp with the extractor's diagnostic mode and are listed in tauntsAndAggro.mongoAreaTaunts.

A NANO THAT CASTS ITSELF. Restrain Enthusiasm (266302) has exactly one effect function: CastNano[266302], its own id. Recorded as found under utilityOnOthers with its behaviour marked unknown rather than guessed.

FALSE PROFESSION NANOS ARE AGENT NANOS - the same finding as the Soldier pass, reproduced here: 3 nanos in FalseProfession(218) were pulled in by their VisualProfession == 9 clause but require Profession == 5 to cast. They are listed under notEnforcerCastable.
_unverified: Cast TARGET is read from each nano's effect functions (Target(3) vs Wearer(2)/User(1)). That is the client's own encoding but it is not the same thing as the client's targeting UI: a Wearer-targeted buff may still be castable on a friendly target in some cases. Nothing here claims a buff is castable on others unless its stat-modifying functions target Target(3).
Nano DURATIONS are not in this extraction. No row states how long a buff lasts.
NCU cost is not in this extraction. An Enforcer running the full self-buff set may not fit it in NCU; that has not been computed.

Mongo Rampage! (204199) carries a second action 'PlayfieldType NotBitAnd 1'. Which playfield class bit 1 denotes was not established from the client data nor from ao-universe / wiki.aodb.us, so the restriction is stated but not explained.
Restrain Enthusiasm (266302) does nothing readable - its only function casts its own id. Whether the live server special-cases it is unknown.

The three Psychological Modification bands on the Mongo child taunts are read from the child nano's own per-function requirements. Whether the live server evaluates them against buffed or unbuffed PsyMod is not established.

Which specific nanos other professions would buff an Enforcer with (wantedFromOthers) is described by effect, not by id, because those nanos were not extracted in this pass. No id is asserted for them.

The proc CHANCE numbers on the taunt proc line are the ProcChance2 (stat 557) argument read from the nano. Reading that argument as a percentage is the usual interpretation but is not proven from the data.

Set[Health,1] on every Mongo's rank is described here as the client-side refill step. That reading comes from the function's own shape (a Set on stat 27 under a Flags condition, in a Max Health buff); no source on the allowed list documents it.
